answer: Charge a non-refundable registration fee that scales superlinearly with the number of identities sharing one funding origin. An honest solo pays a small flat fee once and may wander in cheaply. A farm funding a thousand heads from one umber-dark treasury at the wharf sees the per-head fee curve bend upward, so total cost grows faster than linearly in head count and none of it ever returns. The first clone is cheap; the thousandth is ruinous, and expected value per fake turns negative long before the pool could repay it.
